title: Intelligent qubits
abstract: We introduce the method of ``intelligent qubits,'' which replace live observers in Wigner's friend and Frauchiger--Renner thought experiments, in order to expose the source of the paradoxes: tacit substitution of Boolean hidden variables for non-commuting quantum propositions. The fallacy traces back to London and Bauer's attempt (1939) to legitimize a self-referential interpretation of observers' ``introspection,'' and thus intertwines the measurement and mind-body problems. We cut the Gordian knot by abandoning reductionism, and describe an alternative which fits, we argue, equally naturally with both physics and anthropology takes on the problems.
summary: This paper introduces 'intelligent qubits' to resolve paradoxes in quantum measurement thought experiments. It argues that the conflict arises from mistakenly treating non-commuting quantum properties as if they were classical, definite values. The work proposes abandoning strict reductionism to reconcile quantum physics with observer concepts.
main_problem: The paper tackles the measurement problem in quantum mechanics, specifically challenging the role of the observer and the apparent conflict between unitary evolution and wave function collapse.
main_result: It argues that the paradox stems from a fallacy: treating non-commuting quantum propositions as if they were classical Boolean hidden variables. The solution involves abandoning reductionism regarding the observer's role.
method: The analysis uses thought experiments (like Wigner's friend) and formalisms derived from von Neumann measurements, comparing them to classical mechanics and incorporating environmental decoherence models.
model_or_system: The core model is quantum mechanical systems interacting with measuring apparatuses or observers. The formalism involves state vectors in Hilbert spaces, density matrices, and the comparison between commuting (classical) and non-commuting (quantum) observables.
key_observables: Expectation values of observables, entanglement structure ($\Psi$), mixed density matrix ($P$), and the commutation relations of operators ([p, q] = i\hbar).
important_parameters: Planck constant ($\hbar$), time scales for recurrence vs. cosmic age, and the nature of information loss/retention.
main_assumptions: The paper critiques the assumption that physical reality must be described by a purely objective, counterfactual dynamical universe emerging from unitary evolution alone.
paper_structure: The structure moves from defining the measurement problem via thought experiments to analyzing formalisms (von Neumann/decoherence), identifying the core fallacy regarding hidden variables, and proposing a non-reductionist alternative that integrates physics with anthropology.
why_interesting: It provides a deep conceptual critique of quantum foundations, which is highly relevant for theorists working on open quantum systems, as it questions the very interpretation underpinning decoherence models.
